4.

Date of final order : 08.05.2025  JUDGMENT 1.

The accused person namely Sunil Dutt Sharma is facing trial for offence U/S 323/341 IPC with the allegations that on 15.06.2022 at 05:15 PM in front of RZF-777/20, Gali NO. 16, Raj Nagar-II, Palam Colony, New Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Palam Village, accused person wrongfully restrained the complainant Anil Kumar S/o Sh. Devi Ram and assaulted him causing hurt and thereby accused Sunil Dutt Sharma committed an offence punishable U/s 323/341 IPC.
The criminal law was set into motion by registration of FIR FIR No. 285/2022 St. Vs. Sunil Dutt Sharma against the accused person and investigation into the case began.
After completion of the investigation, the present charge-sheet was filed for conducting trial of the accused person for the alleged offence.
2. After taking cognizance of the offence, the copies of charge-sheet was supplied to the accused person in compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C.
The arguments on charges were heard and charge for offence U/S 323/341 IPC was framed against accused person on 02.03.2023.
The accused person pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Thereafter, prosecution evidence was led.
3. In order to prove allegations against accused, prosecution has examined three prosecution witnesses.
Prior to delving into the contentions raised by the prosecution and defence, let us discuss the testimonies of the material prosecution witnesses in brief.
4. PW-2 Sh. Anil Kumar is the complainant in the present case.

He deposed that on 15.06.2022 at about 01:00 pm, illegal construction was going on RZF- 777/20, Gali No.16, Raj Nagar Part II,
Palam Colony and therefore, he made the call on 112.

At about 05:15 pm, when he was going on his State vs Sunil Dutt Sharma on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101233882/
1 motorcycle to the house of Sh. Vijay Pal Yadav (friend of his deceased father) to give him information about the death of his father who expired on 12.05.2022 and on his way when he was crossing the street of the above mentioned illegal construction site, the accused who was present there, tried to hit him on his head with Fawda (spade tool) but he brought his hand before his head to save himself and therefore, the said Fawda hit on the elbow of his right hand.
Thereafter, he again hit the Fawda on his bike and when the bike did not fell, he hit with the Fawda on his right leg.
Thereafter, he fell down on the road and the accused again tried to hit him with the Fawda but somehow he saved himself from the hits.
FIR No. 285/2022 St.
Vs. Sunil Dutt Sharma
Thereafter, the accused hit the face of complainant with his head.
At that time, it is deposed that accused was drunk thereafter, he fled away from the spot.
He dialed the 100 number.
He was taken to the Indira Gandhi Hospital and thereafter, he moved to DDU hospital.
He gave his statement to the police on next day of the incident at the PS and same is Ex.PW2/A.
Site plan is Ex.PW2/B.

The complainant further deposed that on 02.11.2022, when he was present at the Registrar office, Kapashera and during that time, the accused was also present there and he threatened him to kill him as he had lodged complaint against him.
He made the 112 number call regarding this incident as well.
Accused alongwith Fawda was correctly identified by the witness in the court and the same is Ex. P-1.
During his cross examination by the Ld.

Counsel for accused the witness denied the suggestions that he had filed the false case against the accused as the accused was mentioned as a witness in case FIR No. 494/2019 PS Palam Village, u/s 376/506 IPC and in order to pressurize the accused the complainant has also filed civil case No. CJSCJ/1201/2022 titled as Anil Kumar Vs Sunil Dutt Sharma.

sentences.text: The witness further admitted that he had a call to the PCR at around 12:15 PM or 12:30 PM regarding illegal construction being carried out near his office.
He further denied the suggestions that he picked up the quarrel with the accused by going to his site of illegal construction after making the PCR call.
5. PW-3 ASI Ram Singh is the IO of this case.
He deposed that on 15.06.2022 he was posted as ASI at PS Palam Village.
On that day.

he received DD No.123A regarding quarrel at RZ1777/20, Gali No.
16, Raj Nagar Part II, Palam Colony, New Delhi.

Thereafter he alongwith Ct Ravi reached at the spot and victim was not found at the spot as he was found to be taken to the Indira FIR No. 285/2022 St.

Sharma
Gandhi Hospital
. Thereafter, they left for Indira Gandhi Hospital and from there, he came to know that victim had gone to DDU Hospital for X Ray.
He received the MLC of the victim Anil Kumar from Indira Gandhi Hospital.
On 16.06.2022 victim came to the PS and gave his statement which is already Ex.PWI/A.
He prepared the rukka now Ex.PW3/A.
Thereafter he handed over the rukka to the DO for registration of FIR and after lodging of the FIR, rukka and copy of the FIR was handed over to him.
He prepared the site plan at the instance of the victim at the spot already Ex.PW2/B.
On 17.06.2022 he alongwith Ct Ravi Kumar went to the office of the accused G281, Gali No.6, Raj Nagar Part II, Palam and accused joined the investigation in the present matter.
He recorded his disclosure statement now Ex.PW3/B.
He seized the Fawda used in the incident vide seizure memo Ex.PW3/C.
He formally arrested the accused and conducted his personal search vide memos Ex.PW3/D and Ex.PW3/E.
He obtained the opinion of the doctor on the MLC during investigation.
He recorded the statement of the witnesses during investigation and on completion of investigation, He filed the charge-sheet before the Hon'ble Court.
Accused alongwith Fawda was correctly identified by the witness in the court and the same is Ex. P-1.

During State vs Sunil Dutt Sharma on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101233882/
2
his cross examination, the PW-3/IO ASI Ram Singh that he had not seized the motor cycle or got the same mechanically inspected.
He has further stated that he asked the complainant to produce his bike for mechanical inspection but he did not produced the same.

He further admitted that no blood stain marks were seen on the said Fawda when he seized it vide seizure memo Ex PW3/C.
6.

PW-1 Dr. Ajay Sharma, Senior Medical Officer, Indira Gandhi Hospital, New Delhi was examined by the prosecution to prove the MLC of the FIR No. 285/2022 St. Vs. Sunil Dutt Sharma complainant which was conducted by PW-1 and Dr. Aakash.

PW-1 deposed that the MLC No.763/22 was prepared by Dr. Aakash (Sr) under supervision of PW-1 and as per the MLC and X Ray report,
he opined the nature of injury as simple.
On local examination, some injury was found on the person and they are mentioned at point 1 to 7 on the MI.C. Ex PW-1/A bearing his signature as well as signature of Dr. Aakash at point B.
He identified signature of Dr. Aakash.

STATEMENT OF ACCUSED U/S 313 Cr.P.C.:
7.

Statement of the accused person Sunil Dutt Sharma under Section 281/313 Cr.P.C. was recorded separately on 07.08.2024 in which all the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence were put to him.
The accused person controverted and denied the allegations leveled against him and stated that he has been falsely implicated in the case.

Accused further opted to lead defence evidence and examined himself as DW-1.
8. DW-1

Sh. Sunil Dutt Sharma S/o Sh. Ram Kumar Sharma R/o H No. RZH-796, Raj Nagar II,
Palam Colony, New Delhi
. The accused deposed that the complainant namely Sh. Anil Bhogal used to visit in his neighbourhood in the house of Sarojini Aswal W/o Sh. Sushil Aswal.
The said Sarojini Aswal filed a rape complaint/case FIR NO. 494/2019, PS Palam Village, against the complainant Sh.Anil Bhogal in which he was a prosecution witness.
The complainant Sh. Anil Bhogal remained in judicial custody in the said case for about 4 months.
Thereafter, when he got released from the custody, complainant Sh. Anil Bhogal, started harassing and torturing him and pressurizing not to depose against him in the said rape case.
The complainant had also filed one civil case NO. CS, SCI 1201/2022, against him, which was already dismissed.
The complainant has also filed other several false cases against him.
He has FIR No. 285/2022 St. Vs. Sunil Dutt Sharma further deposed that he not present at the spot on the alleged day of incident i.e. 15.06.2022.
The complainant had sustained injuries by falling on his own because of slipping of his bike.
The said fact of slipping of bike of complainant was told to him by one of my friend later on.
During his cross examination, the accused admitted that police did not record the statement of his friend who told that the complainant sustained injuries due to the slipping of bike.
It is correct that he had not filed any complaint with the police regarding torture or pressure from the complainant side to him pressurizing not to give evidence in Rape Case.

It is pertinent to mention that when the witness was confronted with his statement of accused U/s 313 Cr.P.C recorded on 07.08.2024 wherein while answering question NO.
7 he stated that the complainant was fell down from his bike while he was standing at his house and was trying to remove construction material and while examined as DW-1 the accused mentioned that he was not present at the spot on the date of incident to which the accused admitted that he was not present at the spot.
No other witness was examined in defence and the matter proceeded for final argument.

3 FINAL ARGUMENTS
9. I have heard the Ld. APP for State and counsel for accused person and perused the records of the case.

10. It is argued by the Ld. APP for State that the case of the prosecution has been duly proved by all witnesses examined on behalf of the prosecution and the only irresistible conclusion that can be drawn from the prosecution's evidence is the conviction of the accused person.
11.

On the other hand, it has been argued by Ld. Counsel for accused person that accused person have as been falsely implicated in this case and there is no FIR No. 285/2022 St. Vs. Sunil Dutt Sharma legally sustainable evidence against the accused person to hold them guilty for the offences for which they have been charged in this case FIR as there are contradictions in the testimonies of prosecution witnesses.

APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE AND CONSEQUENT FINDINGS:
12.

Therefore, after going through the evidence and circumstances of the case, it emerges that after the receipt of message regarding DD NO. 123A dt. 15.06.2022, IO ASI Ram Singh Meena/PW-3 reached at the spot of occurrence from where he came to know that the victim was taken to IGI Hospital.

Thereafter, the IO reached the said hospital and obtained MLC NO. 763/2022 Ex PW1/A and recorded the statement of complainant Ex 2/A and the complainant deposed that on 15.06.2022 at around 5:15 PM the accused got hold of the complainant and hit his bike with Fawda.

Thereafter,
he hit the right hand of the complainant with Fawda and assaulted him with his head on his face.
During investigation the IO seized the said Fawda vide seizure memo Ex PW3/C, prepared site plan Ex. PW2/B and thereafter, recorded the disclosure statement of accused Ex. PW3/B.
The IO thereafter, arrested the accused and conducted his personal search vide memo Ex. PW3/D and Ex PW3/E respectively.

The prosecution examined Dr. Ajay Sharma, SMO, IGI Hospital as PW/1 who testified the MLC Ex. PW-1/A and further, stated that after examination of the complainant no bony injury was found and nature of injury was opined to be simple and blunt in nature.

13. During the trial, the prosecution examined Anil Kumar/PW-2 who is the complainant and he testified that on 15.06.2022 at 1:00 PM, he saw the illegal construction going on at RZF 777/20, Gali NO. 16 Raj Nagar-II, Palam Colony, New Delhi and thereafter, made a call at 100 number.

When he was going on his motorcycle from the same area at around 5:15 PM then the accused tried to hit FIR No. 285/2022 St. Vs. Sunil Dutt Sharma him on his head with Fawda but he brought his hand before his head to save himself and therefore, the Fawda hit on the Elbow of his right hand.
Thereafter, the accused again hit with Fawda on his bike and on his right leg.
Thereafter, the accused hit the complainant on his face with his head.

The said testimony of the complainant stands duly corroborated with the nature of injuries as mentioned in MLC Ex PW1/A where the Doctor has observed a contusion on right leg, injury on his arm, swelling on the Elbow, punctured wound over arm, upper lip injury and abrasion over upper part of right leg.
Thus, the nature of injury as alleged by the complainant stands duly corroborated with the MLC of the complainant.

4 14.

It is argued by the Ld. Counsel of the accused that there is no other independent witness examined by the prosecution to support the theory of the complainant and it is argued that no injury was caused by the accused and on the contrary the complainant had fallen from his motor cycle and sustained injuries.

It is further argued that the accused is cited as a witness in FIR No. 494/2019 PS Palam Village u/s 376/506 IPC which is against the complainant and in order to pressurize the accused, the present false case instituted by the complainant.

It is further argued that the accused when appeared as DW1 has also deposed the same to bring out the motive of the complainant to implicate him in the present case and the accused was not even present at the spot of occurrence.
15. The defence taken by the accused does not seem to be probable.

The Ld. Counsel for the accused has himself given a suggestion to the complainant when he appeared as PW 2 that he deliberately picked up the quarrel by going to the site of illegal construction after making the PCR call and the same was denied by the complainant.

In view of the above suggestion the accused has FIR No.
285/2022 St.
Vs. Sunil Dutt Sharma himself admitted that there was a quarrel between the complainant and him at the construction site and thus the presence of the accused at the site stands established.

Further, the accused during his statement u/s 313 CrPC has categorically stated that the complainant had fallen from his bike while the accused was standing in his house and removing the construction material near his house.
Thus, there is an admission by the accused to the extent that he was present at the site of construction when the complainant was also present there.

Though he has taken the defence that the complainant suffered injuries when he had fallen from his motorcycle but when confronted by Ld. Counsel for the complainant during his cross examination when he appeared as DW1, the accused changed his defence given at the time of recording of his statement u/s 313 CrPC and stated that he was not present at the spot but he got to know about the injuries of the complainant due to slipping of his bike as one of his friend had seen the incident.

However, it is pertinent to mentioned that the accused has neither mentioned the name of his friend nor produced him during his evidence to prove that the injury sustained by the complainant was due to slipping of his bike.
Counsel for accused person further argued that no corroborative evidence in any form has come on record and no independent witness is examined by the prosecution.
The labours who were working at the place of incident have not been made witnesses despite the place being a residential locality.

In this regard, it is observed that non examination of public witnesses cannot be considered to be fatal to the prosecution case as it is generally seen that the general public does not come forward to give evidence or get entangled in the criminal investigation and prefers to stay away from the same.
Therefore, it cannot be made a mandate for the prosecution case and give unwarranted FIR No. 285/2022 St. Vs. Sunil Dutt Sharma benefit to the accused when other form of evidence exists.
The sole testimony of injured is also considered sufficient to prove prosecution's case unless and until it suffers from serious defect or infirmity.

In the regard reference can be drawn from the judgment titled as Sadhu Saran Singh v. State of U.P. in Criminal Appeal no. 1467-1468 of 2005,
wherein it was observed by the Apex Court that the case of the prosecution cannot be doubted only on the ground that no independent witness was examined.

The relevant para of the judgment is as follows:
State vs Sunil Dutt Sharma on 8 May, 2025

5 "... 21...
vi) As far as the non - examination of any other independent witness is concerned, there is no doubt that the prosecution has not been able to produce any independent witness.
But, the prosecution cannot be doubted on this ground alone.
In these days, civilized people are generally insensitive to come forward to give any statement in respect of any criminal offence.
Unless it is inevitable, people normally keep away from the court as they feel it distressing and stressful.
Though this kind of human behaviour is indeed unfortunate, but it is a normal phenomena.
We cannot ignore this handicap of the investigating agency in discharging their duty.
We cannot derail the entire case on the mere ground of absence of independent witness as long as the evidence of the eyewitness, though interested, is trustworthy."

17. Therefore, the prosecution has duly proved that the complainant and the accused were present at the spot of incident, the nature of injury sustained by the complainant stands duly corroborated by the prosecution through MLC Ex PW1/A and as observed above, the defence taken by the accused has not been proved beyond reasonable doubt to cast shadow over the deposition of the complainant and the other prosecution witnesses.
The complainant who had sustained injuries will not let the person who had inflicted injuries upon him flee from the hands of justice to implicate some other person.

Therefore, in view of the discussion made above, I am of the considered view that the prosecution FIR No. 285/2022 St. Vs. Sunil Dutt Sharma has duly proved the guilt of accused person namely Sunil Dutt Sharma beyond all reasonable doubts for the offence punishable U/s 323/341 IPC.
18.
Let convict namely Sunil Dutt Sharma be heard on the point of sentence separately.
